title: Extra
description: Documented how to pin a version of one of the Python `tabpfn` library's own dependencies, such as `torch` or `numpy`, when a new release of that dependency breaks a `tabpfn` version that worked before. Use `extra_packages` in `install_tabpfn()` for the persistent environment, or `reticulate::py_require()` for the ephemeral one. See the "Pinning dependencies" section in `?install_tabpfn` (#40).

title: Redirect skrub/torch cache dirs to R_user_dir() instead of $HOME
description:
CRAN flagged that loading this package creates `~/skrub_data`. Python's `skrub` (a `tabpfn` dependency via its `DatetimeEncoder`/`StringEncoder` preprocessing) creates that directory unconditionally at import time.

`.onLoad()` now sets `SKB_DATA_DIRECTORY` to redirect it into `tools::R_user_dir("tabpfn", "cache")`. I also switched the existing `TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR` redirect from `tempdir()` to the same location for consistency, so it persists across sessions instead of rebuilding every time.

I updated test setup/teardown accordingly: `.onLoad()` now sets both vars before `setup.R` runs, so `setup.R` unconditionally overrides them to `tempdir()` during tests instead of only filling them in when unset.

title: Updates TabPFN version
description:
- Test snapshots now record TabPFN v3.5, the model the Python library currently defaults to. They will need updating again whenever that default moves.

- `?tab_pfn` now lists each model version's limits, including the lower one that applies on a CPU, and its examples use current versions rather than earlier ones.

- The `training_set_limit` argument of `tab_pfn()` now defaults to `Inf`, so all of your data is used. It previously sampled anything larger down to 10,000 rows without saying so.

- `tab_pfn()` no longer checks your data against the model's limits; the Python library does, and its error names the model in use. Limits now follow the version you chose rather than one fixed set.

- Failures coming from the Python library are now reported as R errors. The message keeps what the library said and drops the wrapper around it, and `tab_pfn()` adds what to do about it in R, such as lowering `training_set_limit`. This covers `predict()` as well.

Before: 

```r
n <- 50001
d <- data.frame(y = rnorm(n), x1 = rnorm(n), x2 = rnorm(n))
tab_pfn(d[,2:3], d$y, version = "v2.5")
#> Error in `tab_pfn_impl()` at tabpfn/R/TabPFN-fit.R:464:3:
#> ! Model failed: Error in py_call_impl(callable, call_args$unnamed,
#>   call_args$named) : tabpfn.errors.TabPFNValidationError: Number of samples
#>   `50,001` in the input data is greater than the maximum number of samples
#>   `50,000` officially supported by TabPFN. Set `ignore_pretraining_limits=True`
#>   to override this error! Run `reticulate::py_last_error()` for details.
```

After: 

```r
tab_pfn(d[,2:3], d$y, version = "v2.5")
#> Error in `tab_pfn()`:
#> ✖ Number of samples `50,001` in the input data is greater than the
#>   maximum number of samples `50,000` officially supported by TabPFN.
#> ℹ Set `training_set_limit` to fit on a sample, or
#>   `control_tab_pfn(ignore_pretraining_limits = TRUE)` to use every row.
```

- Fixed a failure that stopped models from fitting at all on some setups, reported as `AttributeError: property 'stream' of '_StderrHandler' object has no setter` (#40). The package no longer uses `reticulate::py_capture_output()`, which reassigns the streams of Python's logging handlers and errors when one of them is read-only.

- CI pins `torch` to 2.13.0. The 2.14.0 release triggers the `_StderrHandler` failure above, and the pin stays until that is settled upstream.

title: Captures TabPFN version & device. Accepts bare numbers for `version` arg
description:
## What we did

- Fitted `tab_pfn` objects now record the underlying model version in `$version` and the resolved device(s) in `$device` (both fall back to `"unknown"`).
- Both are shown by the print method, which also got a cleaner header.
- `version` now accepts bare numbers: `2.5`, `"2.5"`, and `"v2.5"` are equivalent (a `"v"` is prepended when missing).

## What it looks like

Print method, before → after:

```r
# before
#> TabPFN Classification Model
#>
#> Training set
#> i 20 data points
#> i 2 predictors
#> i class levels: "a" and "b"

# after
m <- tab_pfn(y ~ ., data = df)
m
#>
#> ── TabPFN-v3 Classification Model ──
#>
#> Training set:
#> ℹ 20 data points
#> ℹ 2 predictors
#> ℹ class levels: "a" and "b"
#> Device:
#> ℹ mps

m$version
#> [1] "TabPFN-v3"
m$device
#> [1] "mps"
```

Version normalization:

```r
tabpfn:::normalize_model_version(2.5)
#> [1] "v2.5"
tabpfn:::normalize_model_version("v2.5")
#> [1] "v2.5"
```

## Why

- **Version/device were invisible after fitting**, so users couldn't confirm which model ran or whether it used GPU/MPS vs CPU — both affect results and speed. Extraction is soft (wrapped in `try()`) so changes to TabPFN's Python internals can't break fitting.
- **Bare version numbers** (`version = 2.5`) are the natural thing to type; the Python library needs `"v"`-prefixed strings. Matching stays exact, so `2.5` won't accidentally match `v2.5-turbo`.

Tests force CPU via a `local_tabpfn_cpu()` helper so the printed device is deterministic in snapshots.

title: Adds install_tabpfn()
description:
## Why

Until now, the `tabpfn` Python library was provisioned implicitly: the first
time the package touched Python, reticulate built an ephemeral environment on
demand. That works, but it leaves end-users with no say over *which* version of
`tabpfn` they run — and no obvious, stable way to lock one in.

That matters because model behavior and results can shift between `tabpfn`
releases. A user who has validated their work against a particular version needs
to be able to stay on it deliberately, and to know that a colleague running the
same code gets the same Python library underneath. An implicit, floating
environment can't offer that guarantee.

This PR gives users a single, predictable entry point for setting up and pinning
their Python environment, so version selection becomes an explicit, reproducible
choice rather than an implementation detail.

## What this enables

- **Pin a version and keep it.** `install_tabpfn(version = "2.0.9")` provisions
  exactly that release into a persistent `"r-tabpfn"` environment that
  reticulate discovers automatically on subsequent sessions.
- **Stay put without being nagged.** By default the function offers to upgrade
  when a newer release exists; `check_latest = FALSE` turns that off for users
  who intentionally want an older, fixed version.
- **No change for everyone else.** Users who don't care about versioning keep
  the zero-config experience — the on-demand environment still works exactly as
  before.

title: Add AutoTabPFN support
description: AutoTabPFN (called "TabPFN (PHE)" in the original [TabPFN paper](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-024-08328-6)) is an ensemble version of TabPFN. It is slower to train and use, but on average yields better predictions, and is "recommended for most use cases" according to the [official documentation](AutoTabPFN). This PR adds support for AutoTabPFN models trained using the [tabpfn-community.post_hoc_ensembles package](https://github.com/PriorLabs/tabpfn-community/tree/main). I've added instructions for training such models at the bottom of the README.

title: Improvements to library load
description:
- In `tab_pfn_impl()`,  the import call now uses the same R object as the one from `.onLoad()`. This ensures that the `check_libomp()` is activated.

title: Adds ability to handle specific versions of TabPFN weight
description:
- `tab_pfn()` gains a `version` argument to select a specific TabPFN model
  version (e.g., `"v2"`, `"v2.5"`). When `NULL`, the Python library's current
  default is used (Fixes #15).
    - TabPFN will automatically download models the first time they are referenced
    - `model <- tab_pfn(mpg ~ ., data = mtcars, version = "v2")` 
    - The reason for the prefixed "v", is because I'm using the raw value used in the TabPFN Python library, so we won't have to write additional code whe new models become available
    - Realized that the main functionality of `create_default_for_version([version])` is to return the local path of the version and type (regressor vs classifier), even if it's not yet downloaded. I just call that function, extract the path, and added it as part of the options passed during the regressor or classifier call 

- New `download_tab_pfn_models()` downloads all available model weights to the
  local cache. Already-cached weights are skipped. 
    - Did not add an argument to customize location, because this is an quick-and-easy function for users easily get all of the models in one call

title: add `download_all_models`
description:
added a function called `download_all_models`, this will pull all pre-trained model checkpoints from Hugging Face. This allows users to point to models other than the default model for classification / regression. 

I updated the control with a model path slot as well to close #15. There are 36 models on Prior Lab's HF at the moment, roughly 1.2GB of pretrained models! 

Below showcases how we might swap to use RealTabPFN-2.5. I think this could be useful as the 'Real' variants typically showcase higher scores on TabArena. Noting that 'Real' is trained on synthetic and real datasets. 

 
```r
library(tabpfn)

# default model regression mode ------------------------
reg_mod <- tab_pfn(
  mtcars[1:25, -1],
  mtcars$mpg[1:25]
)

predict(reg_mod, mtcars[26:32, -1])

# download all chpts ------------------------------------
# get all pretrained models: 
# download_all_models()

cache_dir <- path.expand("~/.cache/tabpfn")
# 36 models! 
all_models <- list.files(cache_dir, recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)

# "real" model regression mode ----------------------------
ctrl <- control_tab_pfn(
 # user specified model path in the control
  model_path = "/home/frankiethull/.cache/tabpfn/tabpfn-v2.5-regressor-v2.5_real.ckpt"
)

reg_mod <- tab_pfn(
  mtcars[1:25, -1],
  mtcars$mpg[1:25],
  control = ctrl
)

predict(reg_mod, mtcars[26:32, -1])

```

title: Modify `reticulate::import()` approach
description:
This PR:
- Replaces eager `reticulate::import()` in individual functions with a `reticulate::import(delay_load = TRUE)` in `.onLoad()`.
- Removes `py_list_packages()` from a hot code path, since assembling a list of all installed Python packages is a potentially expensive operation. 
- Tweak the error message hint, advising users to call `py_install()` if they want to use a self-managed Python installation.
- Remove the Python version constraint in the `py_require()` call. The dev version of reticulate now defaults to selecting the 3rd latest minor Python version, which should alleviate the need for this constraint (and let the `py_require()` call be more future-proof).
